inherits.read: anchorframe/projects/matter-of-light/project.json → final, and workflow.json → stage 8 (Learn): the delivered film ran 100 scenes at 3.7s against a 23-shot board; cuts landed on lyrics; five costume states of the lead reached the jury; the Predictor refused 16s renders; two silent regenerations came back with phantom speech; a wide read adults as children.
lessons_applied: Every shot is 16s or under, and the 16s set pieces (S1, S5, S11, S18, S22, S23) get a 15s take too, so the Predictor can score them.
Audio is off on every silent shot (15 of 26) so the model cannot add speech; the tail of every audio-on take is soloed at Gate E.
Each set piece names its B lane in `notes`; generate it before Gate D. Montage shots are 8–12s because the cut will run short.
The middle cue is diegetic and its lyrics are the screenplay's own, so the board is written to the song instead of discovering it in the cut (tip 32).
One Soul per face before any shot — Ammon and Sadie first. No second design of a lead reaches the board.

Every sheet says 18+ and every wide with a figure in it is read back through the analyser before delivery (tip 34). Matteo is sixteen in the source; the sheet renders him as a young man and S21–S22 keep him in storm light.
No packshot and no title card inside a generated shot; the end card is editorial.
The continuity audit runs on the timeline at Gate E, not on the board.

pace_and_look._: Episode 1's rhythm and grade, read off the delivered cut (final-cut.notes.json) and turned into generation rules for this film.
pace_and_look.rhythm: 100 scenes at 3.6s on average (median 3s); holds of 9-15s only on dialogue and set pieces. Generate montage moments as 8s takes with two beats, inserts as 5s takes, and plan a cut every 3-4s.
rules: One lighting plate per movement, attached to every frame for key direction, colour and contrast (plate-stardust, plate-high-forest, plate-lake-of-light, plate-leviticum), as Episode 1 did with plate-sun and plate-ocean-dark.
Open on the strongest image: the Predictor's hook window is the first 3 seconds, and the first-pass takes that built slowly to their peak scored lowest (S16 46, S5 48).
Dark ground, one bright subject: the best first-pass scores were a figure alone at dawn (S7 66) and a stone glowing in black sand (S22 59).
One accent per world: amber in the High Forest, lime-teal at the lake, candle amber in the Leviticum, violet for Stardust. True blacks; never lift them.
Identity is attached, never described: every face is its element, every take starts from a still made on those elements; adults read as adults in every wide.
High bitrate and model audio off on every take; the song is laid in the edit and the cuts land on its words.

shots.title: Leaving the sun
shots.prompt: Slow crane back, 35mm anamorphic. We open on the white courtyard on the surface of the star where the last film stood (@[courtyard-of-worlds](afc4fc5d-86be-4072-927c-f890966feaca), key light @[plate-sun](03dbcec8-c65f-482c-8c11-58782c673c93)). One point of purer white detaches from the surface and lifts — a blanket of STARDUST, spinning, the purest white there is, leaving particles behind that compress into stars as the camera follows it out of the glare into black space (@[machira-orbit](e7b2e80e-59db-44be-a654-7534a042e2c8)). The star shrinks to one light among many. Hold on the blanket of light moving away, stepping over time. 21:9, photoreal, anamorphic. No text, no captions, no logos anywhere in frame. REFERENCES — attach before generating: @[courtyard-of-worlds](afc4fc5d-86be-4072-927c-f890966feaca); @[plate-sun](03dbcec8-c65f-482c-8c11-58782c673c93); @[machira-orbit](e7b2e80e-59db-44be-a654-7534a042e2c8).

[Intro]
[Spoken Word]
Intelligence is light.
And every light casts a shadow.

[Verse 1]
[Spoken Word]
Before the world there was a word,
a promise spoken into the dark;
every glory, great or small,
was burning from that single spark.
But set a hard heart in the light
and watch the shape it throws:
a shadow born of brightness,
and how the shadow grows.

[Pre-Chorus]
So lift the lantern higher,
don't let it fall behind you...

[Chorus]
Every light casts a shadow,
every shadow knows your name;
the dark was born of brightness,
and it wants the light again.
Hold on to what you're made of,
the sun, the moon, the stars;
every light casts a shadow,
so remember who you are.

[Verse 2]
There's a black seed in the new green ground
where the wave of light came through;
there's a story of a boy who swallowed fire
and the angels that it slew.
The shadow learns to talk like you,
it says you're meant for more,
but the voice that calls you from the storm
is a voice that's lied before.

[Bridge]
Water, Voids, Dominion,
and Energy makes four;
the storm is calling names now,
and it's coming back for more.
Don't answer when it calls you,
don't reach out for its hand;
a shadow needs a light to live,
alone it cannot stand.

[Final Chorus]
Every light casts a shadow,
every shadow knows your name;
the dark was born of brightness,
and it wants the light again.
Hold on to what you're made of,
the sun, the moon, the stars;
every light casts a shadow,
so remember who you are.

[Outro]
[Spoken Word]
Creation began with a single word.
We are one.

learned: Short close inserts beat wides: every 5s insert with one bright subject scored 54-56 (S11 B, S13, S14 B, S16 B), the 8s wides 43-52. The two re-rolls gained 12 and 9 points by opening close on one bright subject — Episode 1's 3-second cut, measured.

Every take peaked at its last second: Cinema Studio builds toward the end of a prompt. Write the peak into the first sentence and the start frame, and cut on the last three seconds when the take still builds.
Lighting plates attach cleanly as elements in both stills and takes; one per movement keeps the grade in one world, as it did in Episode 1.

power._: How power reads on screen, from below the ladder to beyond it. The rungs are Matter of Light's production grammar — its aura grammar, attunement ladder and mind ladder — read against the book, which measures power as understanding and gives no numbered levels ('the source has no levels', film 1's asset register). Book lines carry their chapter; [Matter of Light: …] marks a film-1 reference; anything neither says is marked as a design choice. A shot names its rungs in shots[].tiers as 'who:tier'.
rules: Read the rung from the light, not from effects: where the light sits in the body, how hard its edge is, and what it costs to look at. 'Much suffering was required to reach the level capable of even looking upon one of the Seven Stones' (Ch 01).

An adept's light is bright at the rim and black at the centre; a bearer's is brightest at the centre with no edge [Matter of Light: aura-grammar]. Episode 2 adds a third: a Prison's light is a bearer's core held behind plates of dead stone.

Colour belongs to the Stone, not the rung: Voids is violet and Dominion emerald (Ch 11). Film 1 soured its adepts toward bruise violet and made the Stone of Voids green-white [Matter of Light: ladder-attunement, founding-stone]; from Episode 2 an adept's light goes cold toward steel grey-blue instead, so violet means Voids alone (design choice, from Ch 11). Stardust's light stays white; the violet of Movement I is the sky around it.
Each rung up costs something you can see. The mind buys 'perception of the present, while limiting her foresight' (Ch 02): above sixteen, every split takes colour or sound away.
States are prompt lines, not new elements: attach the character's element and add the rung's prompt line from this table.

endings._: How a bearer's light ends, film 1 against the book, and what Episode 2 does.
endings.book: When Gwendolyn dies the Stone 'fell from her body'; she launched it 'thousands of miles away', 'fell upwards' looking to the Sun 'where she knew Torin was watching', and 'disintegrated' (Ch 02). On Ilan the dying Litiguh leaves 'the same green glow', and 'there was an explosion' (Ch 11).
endings.film1: Matter of Light: scene 67, the kill beat; scenes 80–85, the burst under the cloud and the golden wings — 'the Stone leaves her as wings'. The book has no wings.
endings.episode2: The light ends the house-style way (exploding-angel, then heaven-after); the Stone itself follows the book — it falls, is launched or is taken. Stardust leaves as a slow rising light (S6). The wings stay film 1's signature, kept for a shot that quotes film 1 on purpose.
